In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Nuh (Surah 71)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying]: "Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment."﴾

In this verse is an explanation that Allah, exalted is He, sent His messenger Noah so that he would warn his people before the punishment came upon them. So warning comes first, and it is general across all nations and all messengers.

This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We would not punish until We sent a messenger﴾ [al-Isra' 17:15]. This is for the establishment of proof first, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Messengers as bringers of good news and warners, so that mankind would have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [an-Nisa' 4:165]. The Shaykh, may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him, has already explained this matter in Surah "Bani Isra'il" at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We would not punish until We sent a messenger﴾.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 71, verse 3:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me﴾ ﴿He will forgive you of your sins﴾, and so on. He made obedience here to the Prophet of Allah, Nuh (upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace), and made Allah's forgiving of their sins contingent upon it.

Allah, exalted is He, has already made clear that obedience to the Prophet is obedience to Allah. Thus it is, in its origin, obedience to Allah, because he is a conveyer (muballigh) of what comes from Allah, as in His saying, exalted is He, in Surat an-Nisa': ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and Allah suffices as witness﴾ and ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa': 79–80].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 71, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, indeed I have invited my people night and day."﴾

That is, continuously, as He said: ﴿Then indeed I invited them publicly. Then indeed I announced to them and I confided to them secretly.﴾ [Nuh: 8–9].

That is: the Prophet of Allah, Nuh (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, the prayer and peace), expended everything within his power in the cause of calling to Allah. And He, exalted is He, has specified the duration of his remaining among them in that state in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 14].

(p-307) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They put their fingers in their ears, wrapped themselves in their garments, persisted, and became arrogant with great arrogance.﴾

He, may He be exalted, has made clear the purpose of placing the fingers in the ears, which is so as not to hear, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an."﴾ [Fussilat: 26]. Their persistence and arrogance are only in refusing to follow what Nuh (peace be upon him) called them to.

Like their saying: ﴿And we do not see you followed except by those who are the lowest among us, immature in judgment, and we do not see that you have any merit over us.﴾ [Hud: 27]. Close to this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Burdensome to the polytheists is that to which you call them.﴾ [al-Shura: 13].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 71, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So I said: Ask your Lord for forgiveness; indeed He is ever Forgiving﴾ ﴿He will send down the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾

He has made the sending down of the sky upon them in abundant rain follow upon their seeking forgiveness. This indicates that seeking forgiveness, repentance, and righteous deeds may be a cause of the facilitation of provision.

The Prophet (ﷺ) has also pointed to this in the hadith: "Whoever wishes that his lifespan be extended for him, and that his provision be widened for him, let him maintain the ties of kinship (silat al-rahim)."

The Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) discussed this issue in Surah Hud at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision﴾ [Hud: 3].

Just as the other verse in this surah indicates that disobedience is a cause of destruction, in His saying: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned and then made to enter the Fire﴾ [Nuh: 25].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 71, verse 14:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾, refers to what is made clear in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop [of semen] in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [Yusuf: 12-14].

This meaning is narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was said by Ibn Kathir and al-Qurtubi.

It was also said: "Atwaran" means youth, old age, and weakness.

It was also said: "Atwaran" means types: healthy and sick, seeing and blind, rich and poor.

(p-308) It was also said: "Atwaran" means their differing in character and actions. This was said by al-Qurtubi.

However, as the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him) previously stated, when the interpretations of a verse multiply and there is an indicator in the verse pointing to one of them, then that is to be made clear. Here there is an indicator in the verse that the intended meaning is the first, although all of them are correct. The indicator is that the verse concerns the matter of creation, which is the first bringing into existence, since what follows existence are accidental attributes.

A parallel to this verse has come in Surat al-Mu'minun, as we previously mentioned, and it is concluded with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14].

Among its indications is that the verse is brought to demonstrate Allah's power to resurrect them after their death for recompense, so the most fitting thing is that its subject be the perfection of creation and the capacity to bring into existence.

The most fitting for this meaning is their creation from a drop of mixed fluid and despised water, then its development into a clot, then the development of the clot into a lump, then the creation of the lump into bones, then the clothing of the bones with flesh, then his production as another creation.

It is a striking power and an overwhelming authority.

Similar to it in "al-Waqi'ah": ﴿Have you considered that which you emit? Is it you who create it, or are We the Creator?﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 58-59].

And in "at-Tur" concerning the origin of creation: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾ [at-Tur: 35].

The origin of creation and bringing into existence is the strongest proof of power, and it is with it that the disbelievers are answered, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Destroyed is man; how disbelieving is he!﴾ [Abasa: 17], then He said: ﴿From what thing has He created him? From a drop of semen He created him and determined him﴾ [Abasa: 18-19]. All of that is evidence that what is meant by "atwar" in the verse is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, which is included in Surat al-Mu'minun.

Note.

Clarifying the stages of the creation of man in the manner previously stated is stronger in drawing from the servant the acknowledgment of Allah's power (p-309) over reviving the creation as a whole, because it makes him stand upon several stages of his life and origination, and each stage of them is an independent sign. This guidance is also present in cosmic phenomena, such as heaven and earth: the heaven was smoke and was a joined mass, so He parted them; and the earth was not as it is now. He clarified all of this in His saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create or is the heaven? He constructed it. He raised its height and made it proportionate. And He darkened its night and extracted its brightness. And the earth after that He spread. He extracted from it its water and its pasture. And the mountains He set firmly﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 27-32]. And more comprehensive than all of that is His saying, may He be exalted, in "Fussilat": ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds." And He placed therein firmly set mountains upon its surface and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We have come willingly, obedient." So He completed them as seven heavens within two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection﴾ [Fussilat: 9-12]. Then Allah concluded this complete detailing with His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 12], in which there is a clarification that those stages in the creatures are by a specific determination, and that it is by knowledge and from the Almighty, glorified is He. So it would have been possible for Him to create them all at once, but His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it, "Be," and it is.

However, presenting it in this detailed manner has a greater effect on the soul of the listener and a stronger impact upon him. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 71, verse 15:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ ﴿And made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp?﴾ ﴿And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a [gradual] growth.﴾ ﴿Then He will return you into it and bring you out [again] a [final] bringing forth.﴾ In this verse, together with what precedes it, there are three of the four proofs of resurrection (al-Ba'th) that frequently recur in the Qur'an:

The first: the creation of man: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time."﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79].

The second: the creation of the heavens and the earth: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind.﴾ [Ghafir: 57].

The third: the reviving of the earth after its death: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth stilled, but when We send down upon it rain, it stirs and grows. Indeed, He who gives it life is the Giver of life to the dead.﴾ [Fussilat: 39].

The fourth, which we have not mentioned here, is the actual bringing of the dead to life, like the slain man of the Children of Israel: ﴿So We said, "Strike him with part of it." Thus Allah brings the dead to life.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 73].

The detailed explanation of this has already been given in more than one place by the Shaykh (may Allah's mercy be upon us and upon him). Here, the context of these proofs is to refute those who deny the resurrection. However, in this context there is a problem that appears to be great, namely His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ [Nuh: 15].

If the context is to infer the unseen from the known and observed, then the creation of man in stages is perceptible, observed and accepted, and the bringing forth of man from the earth through feeding him from its plants, its revival after its death, its stirring, and its causing plants to grow are all perceptible matters.

It may be said to the addressee: just as you have witnessed the creation of man from nothing and his development in stages, and you have witnessed the reviving of the dead earth, so Allah, who created you and revived the dead earth for you, is able to return you and bring you out from it [again] in a [final] bringing forth.

But how can one say: just as you have witnessed the creation of the heavens as seven layers, so the One who is capable of that is capable of raising you? The fact is that man has not witnessed the creation of the heavens as seven layers, nor has he seen how Allah created them as seven layers. The difficulty here is how it is said to them: ﴿Have you not considered how﴾ [Nuh: 15].

The "kayf" (how) denotes the state and the form, and they did not witness them, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾ [Al-Kahf: 51].

And how can they infer the unknown to them from what is hidden from them?

Here Ibn Kathir raised a pertinent question, namely his statement: "Tibaqan" means one above another. Is this known through revelation alone, or is it among the matters perceived by the senses, known from the movements (al-Tasyir) and eclipses? I think he means "al-Tasyir" from "al-sayr" (motion), for the seven wandering planets eclipse one another, and the nearest of them is the moon in the lowest heaven. He mentioned the seven planets in the seven heavens, and the words of the people of astronomy (Ahl al-Hay'ah), but he did not address the difficulty with a solution that can be relied upon.

Al-Qurtubi said: His statement, exalted is He, ﴿Have you not considered how﴾ is in the manner of informing, not of direct observation.

As you say: "Have you not seen how I did such-and-such to so-and-so?"

According to al-Qurtubi's statement, the first question arises: if it is in the manner of informing, how can the report be made a proof of another report that is known only through hearing?

The answer to this, in summary, from what the verses of the noble Qur'an indicate, is as follows:

First: Ibn Kathir's question, whether this is received through hearing alone or is among matters perceived by the senses, has no place, because there is no way except transmission alone, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves﴾ [Al-Kahf: 51], that is, Adam. We do not know how he was created, nor how the spirit moved into a lifeless clay body, so that it became a sensing, growing, speaking body.

As for al-Qurtubi's statement that it is in the manner of informing and not of direct observation, this is what the Qur'an testifies to.

The Qur'an also answers the question raised against it, in His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿And He placed therein firm mountains from above it and blessed it and determined therein its sustenance in four days, [equal] for those who ask.﴾ ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly."﴾ ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.﴾ ﴿But if they turn away, say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾ [Fussilat: 9–13]. This is because Allah, exalted is He, here definitely addressed the disbelievers, by His statement: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days"﴾.

He addressed them with detailed matters none of which they witnessed with certainty: the creation of the earth in two days, the determining of its sustenance in four days, His turning to the heaven while it was smoke.

And [the address] His saying to it and to the earth: ﴿Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion.﴾

And their saying: ﴿We come willingly.﴾

And His completing them as seven heavens in two days.

And His inspiring in each heaven its command.

All of that is a detailing of matters they did not witness and knew nothing of, and among them is His completing of seven heavens. So all of it was in the manner of informing the group of disbelievers.

He followed it with His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing﴾. So the requirement of this information and the necessity of this decree from the Exalted in Might, the Knowing, is that they should believe it or accept it. This is a characteristic of every report whose truthfulness is certain, from anyone who is confident in his word, who speaks the report; and because of the strength of its truthfulness it binds its hearer, and its speaker does not care whether the hearer accepts it or turns away from it.

Therefore Allah, exalted is He, said immediately after that: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, that is, after informing them of all of that, so do not concern yourself with them: ﴿say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud."﴾

And since Allah addressed them here with ﴿Have you not considered how﴾, this was a matter, because of the extreme truthfulness of the report about it, like the witnessed, perceptible matter that binds them.

The Sunnah has also come, and clarified that manner: that they are seven layers, with between each heaven and the next a journey of five hundred years, and the breadth of each heaven and the thickness of each heaven a journey of five hundred years.

It may be said: the seeing here regarding the manner is by the eye, perceptibly, but in the person of the Messenger ﷺ on the night of the Isra' and Mi'raj, when he was taken up and saw the seven layers, and he would ask permission for each heaven. The witnessing of one member of the species is like the witnessing of all, so it is as though we all witnessed it, through our belief in his truthfulness (ﷺ) and our knowledge of him (ﷺ) in truthfulness from before. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they followed one whose wealth and children increase him in nothing but loss﴾. Here Allah explicitly states that the people of Noah followed one of whom this is the description, even though wealth ordinarily benefits a person. Allah has also made clear that wealth, in fact, may bring about loss and destruction, as in His words: ﴿Indeed, man transgresses, ﴿because he sees himself self-sufficient﴾﴾ [al-'Alaq: 6-7], meaning that through transgression it becomes destruction.

(p-313) In this verse there is a clear statement that the Prophet of Allah, Nuh (Noah), asked Allah to destroy everyone on the earth, all of them, even though the custom of the Messengers is to be patient with their peoples. It also contains Nuh's report about those who would be born after them, that they would give birth only to a wicked disbeliever. So how could he invoke this curse upon his people, and how could he pass judgment on the generations that would come after?

The Noble Qur'an explains these two matters:

As for the first: he did not invoke this curse upon them until after they had challenged him and he had despaired of them. Their challenge is in their words: ﴿O Nuh, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation, so bring us what you threaten us with﴾ [Hud: 32].

And in His words: ﴿The people of Nuh denied before them, so they denied Our servant and said, "He is a madman," and he was rebuked. So he called upon his Lord, "I am overpowered, so give victory"﴾ [al-Qamar: 9-10].

As for his despair of them: it is based on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36].

As for his report about those who would be born: that they would not give birth except to a wicked disbeliever, this follows from the meaning of the verse mentioned just above. For if none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, then the situation is the same in the present and in the future.

Likewise, by the evidence of *istiqra'* (inductive extrapolation from observed reality), which is a valid proof both in the Shari'ah and by reason. He remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years, and only a few believed with him. They and those with them, apart from others, amounted to no more than the cargo of a ship. This was evidence for him concerning his people, that they had been tested by wealth and would not believe in him. It was also the evidence of the Prophet Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, concerning his people.

As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs adornment and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 88].

So the Prophet Musa reported about his people that they would not believe until they saw the painful punishment. This was drawn from the *istiqra'* of their condition in Egypt, when he showed them the great sign: ﴿So he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned away, striving. Then he gathered [his people] and proclaimed, saying, "I am your lord, the most high"﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 21-24].

And after Allah tested them with what He related to us in His words: (p-314) ﴿So We sent upon them the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people﴾ [al-A'raf: 133].

And His words after that: ﴿When the plague fell upon them, they said, "O Musa, invoke your Lord for us by what He has promised you. If you remove the plague from us, we will surely believe you and send with you the Children of Israel." ﴿But when We removed the plague from them for a term which they were to reach, at once they broke their word﴾ [al-A'raf: 134-135].

Whoever is in such a condition, while Musa observes this from them, there is no doubt that he judges them to be people who will not believe until they see the painful punishment.

Likewise, the evidence of *istiqra'* was for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning his people. It was used to reach a conclusion opposite to that for the other peoples, when he returned from al-Ta'if, and the Thaqif did to him what they did, so they wounded his feet with blood. Jibril came to him with the angel of the mountains, and asked his permission to close the two mountains (al-Akhshabayn) upon them. He said: "No. O Allah, guide my people, for they do not know. Indeed, I hope that Allah will bring forth from their loins one who will say: There is no god but Allah." This was because he ﷺ knew through *istiqra'* of their condition that they did not know, and they refrained from belief because of their lack of learning, and that they were in need of instruction.

So when they were taught, they learned, and their nature is receptive to teaching, unlike others who are obstinate in their persistence. For he witnessed among their elders that when the Qur'an was presented to them, and they were addressed with appeals to reason, and they understood what was addressed to them, and were free from fanaticism and other impulses, they responded immediately, as happened to Umar and others, may Allah be pleased with them. Except for those whom Allah informed about their condition, such as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira: ﴿Leave me with the one whom I created alone. And to whom I granted extensive wealth, and sons present with him, and made life smooth for him. Then he desires that I should add more. No! Indeed, he has been stubborn toward Our verses. I will overwhelm him with a steep climb﴾ up to His words ﴿I will burn him in Saqar﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 11-26]. So he ﷺ knew his condition and his end, and for this reason he invoked a curse upon him on the day of Badr.

Similarly Abu Lahab, when his condition became clear through Allah's words: ﴿He will burn in a fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾ [al-Masad: 3-4].

Because the Arabs were a people of natural disposition (*fitrah*), and because Islam is also the religion of *fitrah*, the response to it was closer.

Consider the period of his stay ﷺ from the beginning of his prophethood until his passing to the Highest Companion, twenty-three years. How many embraced Islam during it, while Nuh, peace be upon him, remained a thousand years less fifty years, and only a few believed with him.

(p-315) For this reason Nuh's statement, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, "and they will not give birth except to a wicked disbeliever," was based on *istiqra'* of his people. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

As for His words, ﴿And Nuh said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dwelling one"﴾, it does not state here whether his prayer was answered or not. He clarified this in other places, among them His words: ﴿And Nuh, when he called before, so We responded to him﴾ [al-Anbiya': 76].

And in this same surah, directly before this verse, His words: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned and then entered a Fire, and they found for themselves besides Allah no helpers﴾ [Nuh: 25]. So Allah combined for them the two most extreme punishments: drowning and burning, in exchange for the two greatest sins: misguidance and leading others astray.

Likewise the Exalted described how He destroyed his people and saved him, his family, and those with him, in His words: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overpowered, so give victory." So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water, and We caused the earth to burst forth with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed. And We carried him on a [vessel] of planks and nails, running under Our eyes﴾ [al-Qamar: 10-14], to the end of the verse.

Ibn Kathir said: Allah drowned every disbeliever on the face of the earth, until even the son of Nuh, from his own loins. Here there is an indication regarding the matter of Nuh's son in His words: ﴿"O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers." He said, "I will take refuge in a mountain to protect me from the water." [Nuh] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He gives mercy." And the wave came between them, and he was among the drowned﴾ [Hud: 42-43], when parental compassion overcame Nuh regarding his son. Then he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my son is of my family﴾, to His words: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family﴾ [Hud: 45-46]. Some people raised a question about this in the reading: ﴿Indeed, he is [doing] other than righteous work﴾ [Hud: 46], meaning: indeed, it is an ongoing action, that is, by his disbelief.

They also questioned the validity of his lineage. The truth is that Allah the Exalted protected the wives of the Prophets out of honour for them, and that he was truly his son. For when he said: ﴿Indeed, my son is of my family﴾, this statement contained two matters: his attribution to him in sonship, and secondly his attribution to him in family. So the answer from Allah was the negation of the second attribution, not the first: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family.﴾ He did not say, "Indeed, he is not your son." Family is more general than son, and it is known that negating the more specific does not necessitate negating the more general, and the reverse is the same. So when He negated his attribution to his family, we know that his attribution to him through sonship remains. Had he not been his son by his loins, the negation would have fallen upon that.

It is said: "He is not your son," and when sonship is negated from him, his attribution to his family is negated too. Likewise His words, the Exalted, after it: (p-316) ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾ [Hud: 37], meaning: because the wrongdoers are not of the family with respect to religion, since religion binds the distant, while wrongdoing, which means disbelief, separates the near. And knowledge is with Allah the Exalted.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Nuh

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and not beget except wicked disbelievers.﴾

This noble verse indicates that Nuh, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace, knew what their children would come to of wickedness and disbelief before they were born. Other verses have come indicating that the unseen (al-ghayb) is known only to Allah, such as His saying: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾ [an-Naml: 65].

And like the saying of Nuh himself, as Allah related it about him in Surah "Hud": ﴿And I do not say to you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen﴾ [Hud: 31], to the end of the verse.

The answer to this is clear: he knew, by revelation from Allah, that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed, as He explained by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾ [Hud: 36], to the end of the verse.
